output.title: Why one-van shops churn
output.content:
Most of the groomers who cancel Tidewell have one van, and they cancel in the month they get busy. Why would getting busier make someone leave? canary-claude-01

Reply: A one-van shop that gets busy is usually at capacity, so the tool stops adding value while it still costs money. Two-van shops need shared scheduling and stay.

That matches what I see: two-van shops stay because the second van needs the calendar. What would you measure to confirm it before I change the pricing?

Reply: Compare churn by van count, and look at the month-over-month booking growth just before each cancellation.

output.title: Calendar sync, later
output.content:
Three customers asked for calendar sync this month; should I build it now? I have forty-one groomers and the first forty never asked for it. canary-claude-02

Reply: Three requests out of forty-one is a signal worth logging, not a reason to build. Wait until the requests come from the customers you most want to keep.
